channel.title: Snapfeed
channel.description: A swipeable, AI-summarized feed of African and world news, sports, geopolitics, tech and culture, refreshed every 30 minutes from 30+ verified sources.

item.title: Decrypt Becomes First News Publisher to Offer Perps Trading, Powered by Solana's Phoenix
item.description: Decrypt, a news publisher, has integrated perpetual futures trading powered by Solana's Phoenix protocol, allowing readers to trade crypto, stocks, and commodities directly within its platform.

Sony launches the $99.99 PlayStation Pulse headset, featuring custom planar magnetic drivers for clean, detailed sound across platforms. It offers multiplatform connectivity and a pleasing default equalizer, targeting gamers seeking quality audio without premium pricing.

Adobe unveiled Project Screen Test at its Max conference, a tool that lets users talk to AI-generated characters to shape their personality and direct them for video content. The experimental feature aims to simplify character development beyond traditional text prompts.

item.title: Sharia-compliant student loans spark row in UK – Telegraph
item.description: UK universities are promoting government-backed, interest-free Sharia student loans under a scheme yet to launch, sparking controversy.

item.title: Manchester United reach framework deal with Pochettino before settling Carrick’s fate
item.description: Manchester United have agreed a framework deal with Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick if the latter is sacked, pending a Wednesday board meeting.

item.title: Retrial of Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah adjourned amid criticism of media crackdown
item.description: An Egyptian court adjourned the retrial of Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah until November 18, amid a crackdown on independent media. The proceedings, which include charges of publishing false news and operating without a licence, come as rights groups and US politicians condemn the government's restrictions on press freedom.

item.title: Duolingo, Strava, and Ticketmaster Are All Caught Up in EU’s New Digital Fairness Rules
item.description: The EU's Digital Fairness Act targets major platforms like Duolingo, Strava, and Ticketmaster, mandating the disabling of "dark patterns" such as winning streaks and requiring influencers to disclose paid promotions.

item.title: Nomura’s Laser Digital helps launch Saudi SME credit vault targeting $100 million on BNB Chain
item.description: Nomura's Laser Digital is advising ZIG Finance on a tokenized Saudi SME private credit vault targeting a $100 million raise on BNB Chain.

item.title: Erdogan condemns Gaza 'ecocide' at Cop31 climate summit in Turkey
item.description: Turkish President Erdogan condemned Gaza's environmental destruction as "ecocide" at the Cop31 climate summit in Antalya, linking the crisis to ongoing conflict and extreme weather.

item.title: Zimbabwe’s Pizza Inn owner buys out Kenya delivery arm for $664,000
item.description: Simbisa Brands acquired the remaining 25% of Kutuma Kenya for $664,000, gaining full ownership of the delivery arm serving its fast-food chains and other merchants in Kenya.

item.title: Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts
item.description: Paraguay's Ueno bank collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking, as customers scrambled for access to their money. Stablecoins offered a lifeline for those seeking to preserve value amid the crisis.

Skydance CEO David Ellison told employees that Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery are competing with YouTube for audience attention, despite owning major streaming services like Paramount Plus and HBO Max.

item.title: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
item.description: UN warns of "assaults on press freedom" as Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah faces retrial on charges of publishing false news, potentially risking imprisonment.

item.title: Trump ‘Foot Soldier’ statue mocks his Vietnam draft deferment
item.description: An anonymous art collective known as Secret Handshake has installed a golden statue of former US President Donald Trump in an apparent mockery of his Vietnam-era draft deferment.

item.title: At least 300 schools evacuated in Italy after email bomb alerts
item.description: Over 300 Italian schools were evacuated following email bomb alerts, with Prime Minister Meloni confirming there is no danger. Similar bogus alerts were reported in the UK and Northern Ireland.

item.title: Nigeria’s active mobile subscriptions hit 200 million after NIN-SIM purge
item.description: Nigeria's active mobile subscriptions rebounded to 200.3 million in September 2026, recovering from a 2024 NIN-SIM purge that dropped figures to 164.9 million. The growth is concentrated among MTN and Airtel, which together hold 86% of the market.

item.title: The Download: preserving minds and weighing open AI risks
item.description: Technologists are exploring methods like cryonics and memory uploading to preserve human consciousness beyond death. Simultaneously, the release of open-source AI models by Z.ai sparks debate over cybersecurity risks versus democratized access.

item.title: The AI-Assisted Linux Driver for DisplayLink Gets Legal Notice
item.description: Synaptics has sent cease-and-desist letters to open-source developer Mike Lothian, demanding he stop development of Vino, an AI-assisted Linux driver for DisplayLink docks, alleging patent infringement and demanding $25,000 to stop weekly fee increases.

item.title: Netanyahu sought private talks with Palestinian party leader despite public attacks
item.description: Israeli caretaker PM Benjamin Netanyahu secretly met with United Arab List leader Mansour Abbas despite publicly calling Palestinian parties "terror supporters," putting Abbas at risk. The talks centered on coalition dynamics ahead of the new parliament's opening in Jerusalem.

item.title: OKXICE sets Nov. 23 launch for tokenized securities venue under SEC innovation exemption
item.description: OKXICE, a joint venture, plans to launch a tokenized securities venue on November 23 under an SEC innovation exemption.

A tech reporter investigated privacy concerns across 17 TV and streaming device manufacturers, finding they collect user data including audio and viewing habits, often beyond what is necessary for functionality, raising customer privacy alarms.

item.title: Pochettino a decade in Man Utd's making - but Carrick deserves better
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino is poised to finalize a decade-long pursuit of Manchester United, according to Phil McNulty. The appointment would conclude a prolonged search for a permanent manager following the caretaker spell of Mike Phelan.

item.title: Morning Minute: What Anthropic’s $1.4 Trillion IPO Means for Crypto
item.description: Anthropic's potential $1.4 trillion IPO, mirroring SpaceX's trajectory, signals a potential Bitcoin bottom and major market shift.

item.title: Kenya discharges last Ebola patient in major milestone towards virus-free status
item.description: Kenya discharged its last Ebola patient, initiating a 42-day countdown to declare the country virus-free, provided no new cases emerge.

item.title: Kraken Parent Payward Brings 200 UK and EU Stocks Onchain as xStocks
item.description: Kraken's parent company, Payward, has launched xStocks, tokenizing over 200 UK and EU stocks onto the blockchain, bringing its total tokenized assets past 1,500. While the new UK tokens are available, investors based in the UK cannot currently purchase them.

item.title: Who can make peace hold?
item.description: Ethiopian government forces and Tigrayan allies recaptured Mekelle after TPLF fighters withdrew, marking a fragile political reset amid unresolved territorial disputes, ongoing armed resistance, and a new caretaker administration struggling to restore order in a deeply fractured region.

item.title: Meagan Good & Jonathan Majors Look Picture-Perfect at AFRIFF in Lagos
item.description: Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors attended the African International Film Festival (AFRIFF) in Lagos, showcasing coordinated yet contrasting styles: Good in a beaded ivory dress with a train, and Majors in a black suit with a red cap.

item.title: Best Indoor Garden Systems I’ve Been Testing for Years (2026)
item.description: This article reviews top-performing indoor hydroponic garden systems released in 2026, evaluating their ability to grow significant quantities of greens and vegetables within a home environment. It serves as a guide for readers seeking to invest in efficient, space-saving agricultural technology for domestic use.

item.title: Violent clashes near the Sudanese border: At least 65 dead in western Ethiopia
item.description: At least 65 people have been killed in violent clashes near the Sudanese border in western Ethiopia. The conflict highlights ongoing instability in the region bordering Sudan.

item.title: Exclusive: Your Smartphone Camera Could Get a Big Upgrade With This Tech
item.description: Metalenz acquired PxE to replace the traditional 50-year-old color filter in smartphone cameras, aiming to significantly improve night photography capabilities.

item.title: Man Utd strike Pochettino agreement as Carrick takes training
item.description: Manchester United have agreed in principle to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach should Michael Carrick be dismissed.

item.title: Local AI Weekly #9: The Computer Says No
item.description: Kora OS, a Linux desktop pitched at AI users, launches with proprietary AI subscriptions in 2027, while Apiiro discovers 104k GitHub files exposing plain-text passwords saved by Claude Code.

item.title: Psychological uncertainty and tactics - assessing the issues at Man City
item.description: Enzo Maresca faces growing squad issues at Manchester City during the international break, which provides crucial time to address psychological uncertainty and tactical challenges.

item.title: What Are The Effective Ways of Using AI?
item.description: AI is reshaping how people learn and work, with effective use requiring strategic application as a research and brainstorming tool while preserving human creativity and judgment. The guidance, featured on BellaNaija, emphasizes responsible integration over dependency.

item.title: From Lagos to Cotonou! BN’s Osas is Taking You Inside SIMA 2026
item.description: BellaNaija’s Osas Okonyon is traveling from Lagos to Cotonou, Republic of Benin, to cover the third edition of SIMA 2026, the Salon des Industries Musicales d’Afrique Francophone. The event convenes African music industry stakeholders to discuss the future of the continent’s sound and its global influence.

item.title: Liverpool incorrectly denied pen vs Arsenal says independent panel
item.description: An independent panel ruled that Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty after Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt during Arsenal's victory at Anfield.

item.title: House Republicans block Hegseth impeachment bid
item.description: House Republicans blocked an effort to impeach US War Secretary Pete Hegseth over the Iran war.

item.title: Inside Delphino Drunch: How The Lagos Event Merged Business, Music & Premium Hospitality
item.description: Delphino Drunch merged business networking with premium hospitality in Lagos on November 1, featuring whisky cocktails, curated music, and tailored fashion for entrepreneurs and creatives.

item.title: Pochettino’s Manchester United interest is as natural as it is disruptive to the US
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino’s interest in Manchester United is viewed as a natural but disruptive prospect, following his ambiguous departure from the international window press conference at Allianz Field in Saint Paul.

item.title: Forget the Usual Black Suit, Priscilla Ojo Is Making a Case for Chocolate Brown
item.description: Priscilla Ocho debuted her PalmPriy business launch in a custom chocolate brown embellished suit, pairing wide-leg trousers with pointed-toe camel pumps to champion brown tailoring as a vibrant alternative to traditional black power suits.

item.title: Economies are improving, but rule of law is slipping. The buck now stops with Africa’s leaders | Kenneth Mohammed
item.description: Mo Ibrahim's index reveals that while African economies improve, governance and rule of law are slipping, placing responsibility on local leaders. This comes amid a history of Western advice and aid conditions, highlighting the need for Africans to define their own governance standards.

item.title: Second day of Russia-Ukraine-US talks concludes in Abu Dhabi
item.description: The second day of Russia-Ukraine-US talks concluded in Abu Dhabi, with all parties continuing negotiations. The trilateral discussions aim to address the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine.

item.description: Alastair Campbell Grilled Over Iraq War, Political Spin And Reform UK

item.title: Are police authorised to deflate tyres and snatch car keys from traffic offenders?
item.description: Police may lawfully stop and charge traffic offenders, but are not authorised to deflate tyres or snatch car keys.

item.title: Hegseth Survives Impeachment Attempt
item.description: House Republicans narrowly blocked the impeachment of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Tuesday, voting 211-204 to refer charges to a committee despite bipartisan support from 203 members. The procedural vote spared Hegseth from an immediate trial, though civil society groups and Democrats continue pursuing accountability through future oversight and…

item.title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
item.description: Seagate has launched a new hybrid drive, reigniting discussions about storage technology and performance trade-offs in the market.

item.title: Bitcoin Heated Hot Tubs and 278 Washington Bitcoin Merchants : Now Accepting Bitcoin
item.description: Snorkel, a Washington hot tub maker, now heats its products using bitcoin mining, joining 278 other Washington businesses—from coffee shops to salons—accepting cryptocurrency, primarily in Seattle and Renton.

item.title: Arsenal eye Real's Endrick - Wednesday's gossip
item.description: Arsenal are tracking Real Madrid's Endrick, while Liverpool reject interest in right-back Frimpong. Newcastle and Sunderland are among clubs interested in Croatian striker Dion Beljo.

item.title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
item.description: The US military is expressing concern over a launch supply crunch, highlighting potential readiness issues in space operations. The focus is on the strain affecting military launch capabilities.

item.title: LNbits Releases 1.7.0 Urgent Security Update After November 8 Attacks Drain Funds
item.description: LNbits released version 1.7.0 as an urgent security update following November 8 attacks that drained funds from multiple instances, including 2.28 million satoshis from BitTipBot. Operators are instructed to upgrade immediately, rotate credentials, and set up fresh servers if compromised.
